chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Leon Collins's kid band; Cecil Scott at the Congo Roof Garden
summary: Thomas took a trolley across to East St. Louis and Collinsville to play with Leon Collins and his brother's young band, which was received well and paid. Thomas says he left St. Louis about 1930. At the Congo Roof he met the baritone-playing Joe Thomas and Earl Carruthers. Cecil Scott, nicknamed Doggie, led for about eight months.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

Radio. Remember? Radio was very big in those days. He was the drummer. We used to call him "Doggie".

I don't know. He looked like a doggie. Another Cecil I worked with Cecil Scott, we was in New York, playing those gigs but that was on gigs.
